static_traits.name: Liang Shufang
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues strained by frequently seeking recognition for knitting; have a few close friends but have not yet discussed inferiority feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: No similar inferiority feelings before; have not yet received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, with fairly good logic; attitude negative, with strong self-criticism; willing to try but holds a skeptical attitude; tends to seek others' approval; feels embarrassed about discussing personal problems with others and avoids it

basic_info.main_problem: Because I did not win first place in a knitting competition, I persistently feel I am a 'terrible knitter', triggering marked inferiority and self-criticism, affecting Work focus, Interpersonal relationships and daily self-care.
basic_info.core_demands: 'I just want to feel capable rather than a total failure. I want to enjoy knitting again, not let these negative thoughts overwhelm everything.'; 'These feelings of inadequacy affect my self-esteem and overall well-being, so I seek counseling.'

core_beliefs: I am not good enough (in knitting)
My worth depends on whether I win first place

special_situations.event: Knitting competition results announced, did not win first place
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not won first place, it means my knitting is terrible, I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Putting great pressure on myself to perform, doubling practice to improve skills
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am such a terrible knitter / I failed

special_situations.event: Each time picking up knitting needles or thinking of this competition
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I knit again, I will fail again, proving I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive self-criticism; avoids discussing with close friends to prevent embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time will be terrible too; I will fail again

special_situations.event: Frequently seeks recognition for his knitting when interacting with colleagues, which strains relationships
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' evaluations determine my ability and worth; if they do not approve, I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly seek external recognition from colleagues, avoid independent evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think my knitting is not good enough / look down on me

special_situations.event: Recalling the time and effort invested after not winning first place
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If effort has not brought first place, all the effort does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negate my own progress and strengths
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: All my efforts were wasted, nothing counts

core_conflict.wish: Long to be seen as capable and Gaining recognition (especially in knitting)
core_conflict.fear: Fear of failure and being negated, leading to collapsed self-worth and shame
defense_goal: Avoid failure with high standards and Self-monitoring
Relieve insecurity by seeking external recognition
Avoiding discussing with friends to prevent embarrassment and shame

object_relations.object_representation: Others who will belittle her problems and consider them trivial

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to explore and restructure the rigid belief of 'must win', or to set more realistic goals
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these negative thoughts are 'very real and hard to change', holding a skeptical attitude toward change
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a gentle yet steady tone, acknowledge the truth of their feelings, while distinguishing experience from facts; use concrete examples to Guidance them through small-step experiments, avoiding confrontational persuasion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they share these inadequacy and shame feelings with close friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing knitting issues are 'too trivial, not worth discussing', thus avoiding sharing
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Adopt a normalizing and de-stigmatizing tone, emphasize the impact of the problem on their well-being; use open-ended questions to invite recollections of the support that might be gained after sharing, and encourage attempting a limited degree of self-disclosure.

manifestations: Feeling 'all investment wasted' after not winning first place
Compares knitting with others' more serious problems, believing my distress is 'very trivial'
Self-worth depends excessively on external judgment (competition results, colleagues' approval)
outcomes: Persistent self-criticism and a sense of failure

manifestations: Binding oneself with rigid rules such as 'must win first place'
Loses flexibility of choice under high expectations and high pressure

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Judging oneself by the rule that 'only winning first place counts as good'
Treats competition results as the sole standard of ability and worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Dare not discuss with close friends, managing self-exposure with excessive caution

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Uses 'knitting problems are trivial' as a reason to avoid talking with others about real feelings
When talking about failure emotions, turning to explaining the competition environment/judges' tastes

positive_force: Investing time and energy in knitting, with motivation to learn and improve
Able to clearly express own thoughts and feelings
Willing to try change with small-step goals
Has several close friends who could potentially support
negative_force: Strong self-criticism leads to Impaired self-esteem and avoiding sharing

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent self-criticism and sense of failure (around knitting performance)
antecedent: Seeing or picking up knitting needles
Thinking about the knitting competition and its outcome
When interacting with colleagues and seeking recognition for knitting
target_behavior.core_reason: Equate competition results with self-worth, forming black-and-white and catastrophic cognitions, triggering Self-denial and shame
target_behavior.function: Escape failure and shame, seeking external recognition to briefly relieve insecurity
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased work focus, colleague Relationship tension, Daily self-care affected, further damaged self-esteem
